newsitem.title: USA: Former Fla. Lazard banker aiding U.S. bond probe.
newsitem.headline: Former Fla. Lazard banker aiding U.S. bond probe.

text.p: A former Lazard Freres & Co. banker in Florida is cooperating in a federal investigation of a municipal bond deal the firm was involved in the Atlanta area in the early 1990s, a consultant who is a friend of the banker said Wednesday.

"Jim Eaton is actively cooperating in an ongoing federal investigation into a bond deal in Atlanta from the early '90s," said Ron Sachs, a longtime friend and consultant who said Eaton requested his help in handling media inquiries. "It involves a deal that Lazard Freres was involved in in Atlanta."

Eaton, a former Lazard banker and former campaign manager for Republican U.S. Sen. Bob Graham of Florida, is president and owner of the Tallahassee lobbying firm Capital Strategies. He is prohibited from discussing the ongoing criminal investigation.
"I believe he is not the target of the investigation but he is fully cooperating," Sachs said. "The government has asked him not to talk publicly about the case."
Sachs said he believed the investigation was being conducted by the U.S. Attorney's office in Atlanta.
John Davis, the chief of criminal investigations in the Atlanta office, told Reuters, "I cannot confirm or deny anything about that investigation."

Eaton left Lazard Freres in 1993 when he bought Capital Strategies from Bud Chiles, the son of Florida Gov. Lawton Chiles. The firm handles government and public relations and is not involved in the municipal bond business, said Sachs, a media consultant and television producer who was previously Gov. Chiles' press spokesman.

Lazard Freres left the municipal bond business in December 1995, two months after the firm paid a $24 million fine to the Securities and Exchange Commission for failing to disclose to its clients a fee-splitting arrangement with another investment bank.

In August 1996, former Lazard Freres partner Mark Ferber was convicted in a federal court in Boston of 58 counts of fraud and corruption for his involvement with the fee arrangement. He is appealing the verdict.

Previously, municipal officials and others involved in bond deals in the Atlanta and Jacksonville, Fla., areas have said they received subpoenaes or requests from the SEC for documents from bond deals involving Lazard Freres in the early 1990s.
The SEC has declined to comment on the probe.
